problem: The compensating factors for a moved take-off point are reversed. Moving a take-off point from before G to after G means it now taps GX, so the branch needs 1/G to recover X, not G. Moving it from after G to before G means it now taps X, so the branch needs G, not 1/G. As written, the trap contradicts Section 2 and the answer to Q4.
fix: A branch taken before G must get 1/G if moved after G (the tapped signal is GX there, so divide by G to keep X); a branch taken after G must get G if moved before G (the tapped signal is X there, so multiply by G to keep GX).
